'''Jean-Louis Scartezzini''' (born 1957 in [[Lausanne]]) is a Swiss building physicist specialized in [[Daylighting (architecture)|day lighting]] and solar buildings. He is a professor of physics at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] (École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne) and the head of the Solar Energy and Building Physics Laboratory (LESO-PB) since 1994.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home Solar Energy and Building Physics Laboratory|url=https://leso.epfl.ch/|access-date=2021-02-05|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Ecucation ==
Scartezzini studied both physics at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] and [[geophysics]] at the [[University of Lausanne]], and obtained his [[Master's degree|Masters's degrees]] in 1980 and 1981, respectively. As a PhD student he joined the Solar Energy Research Group of [[André P. Faist]] at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]], and in 1984 for a year the Solar Energy Application Laboratory (SEAL) at [[Colorado State University]] as a [[visiting scholar]]. He graduated from [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] at the Department of Physics in 1986 with a PhD thesis on "Application of Stochastic Methods to the Analysis of Solar Energy Systems."<ref>{{Cite thesis|last=Scartezzini, Jean-Louis|date=1986|title=Application des méthodes stochastiques à l'étude des systèmes de captage de l'énergie solaire|journal=Infoscience|language=en|doi=10.5075/epfl-thesis-627}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Scartezzini|first1=J.-L.|last2=Faist|first2=A.|last3=Liebling|first3=Th.|date=December 1987|title=Using Markovian stochastic modelling to predict energy performances and thermal comfort of passive solar systems|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0378778887900156|journal=Energy and Buildings|language=en|volume=10|issue=2|pages=135–150|doi=10.1016/0378-7788(87)90015-6|bibcode=1987EneBu..10..135S |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Bottazzi|first1=F.|last2=Liebling|first2=Th.M.|last3=Scartezzini|first3=J.-L.|last4=Nygård-Ferguson|first4=M.|date=January 1991|title=On a Markovian approach for modeling passive solar devices|url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/037877889190003L|journal=Energy and Buildings|language=en|volume=17|issue=2|pages=103–116|doi=10.1016/0378-7788(91)90003-L|bibcode=1991EneBu..17..103B |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

==Career==
He joined the Windows and Lighting Program at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory]] in California as a post-doctoral fellow in 1988 to work on daylighting and green lighting technologies, and air infiltration and ventilation.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Jean-Louis Scartezzini|url=https://people.epfl.ch/jean-louis.scartezzini|website=EPFL}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Michel|first1=L.|last2=Roecker|first2=C.|last3=Scartezzini|first3=J-L.|date=1 December 1995|title=Performance of a new scanning sky simulator|url=http://lrt.sagepub.com/cgi/doi/10.1177/14771535950270040401|journal=Lighting Research and Technology|language=en|volume=27|issue=4|pages=197–207|doi=10.1177/14771535950270040401|s2cid=110445460|issn=1477-1535|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Scartezzini|first1=J-L.|last2=Compagnon|first2=R.|last3=Reecker|first3=C.|last4=Michel|first4=L.|date=1 December 1997|title=Bidirectional photogoniometer for advanced glazing materials based on digital imaging techniques|url=http://lrt.sagepub.com/cgi/doi/10.1177/14771535970290040201|journal=Lighting Research and Technology|language=en|volume=29|issue=4|pages=197–205|doi=10.1177/14771535970290040201|s2cid=110804844|issn=1477-1535|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

From 1990 to 1997, he was associate professor of building physics at the School of Architecture and the University Center for the Study of Energy Problems at the [[University of Geneva]]. In 1994, he was nominated associate professor of building physics at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]], director of the Solar Energy and Building Physics Laboratory and co-director of Institute of Building Technology (ITB) at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]]'s Departement of Architecture. Upon his appointment as full professor at [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne|EPFL]] in 1999, he founded and headed the Institute of Infrastructures, Resources and Environment (ICARE) of the School of Environmental, Architectural and Civil Engineering (ENAC), as well as the Doctoral Program in Environment of EPFL.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Perera|first1=A. == Research ==
Scartezzini's research focuses in an interdisciplinary manner on energy efficiency and application of renewable energies in buildings and neighborhoods. His main working areas are dedicated to the integration of [[Daylighting (architecture)|daylighting]] and [[electric light]]ing;<ref>{{Cite Drawing on various scientific fields, Scartezzin's research facilities maintain a nanotechnological laboratory for solar energy conversion,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Nanotechnology for Solar Energy Conversion|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/leso/research/domains/nano_solar_conversion/|access-date=2021-02-10|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> experimental testbeds, such as the LESO solar experimental building,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Experimental Building|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/leso/research/resources/leso_building/|access-date=2021-03-30|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> a daylighting and photo-biological laboratory,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Integrated Day and Electric Lighting|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/leso/research/domains/daylight_perception/|access-date=2021-02-10|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> and an urban climate monitoring station.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Current research topics|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/leso/research/domains/|access-date=2021-02-10|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref> He is also involved in the development of computer modelling software for design, analyses and [[optimal control]] of buildings and cities.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Urban data mining, intelligence and simulation|url=https://www.epfl.ch/labs/leso/research/domains/urbanenergysystems/|access-date=2021-02-10|website=www.epfl.ch|language=en-GB}}</ref>

Scartezzini is author or co-author of several books related to daylighting and green lighting, such as ''Changing Perspectives on Daylight: Science, Technology and Engineers'' (Science/AAS, 2017), ''Daylight Design of Buildings: a Handbook for Architects and Engineers'' (Routledge, 2002),<ref>{{Cite book|last=Baker|first=Nick|title=Daylight design of buildings|date=2002|publisher=James & James|others=Koen Steemers|isbn=1-873936-88-5|location=London|oclc=50446797}}</ref> ''Daylighting Design: A Source Book on Daylighting Systems and Components'' (LBNL, 2000);<ref>{{Cite web|title=Daylight in Buildings: A Source Book on Daylighting Systems and Components {{!}} Facades|url=https://facades.lbl.gov/daylight-buildings-source-book-daylighting-systems|access-date=2021-03-30|website=facades.lbl.gov}}</ref> ''Lighting Principles; Office Lighting; Industrial Lighting; and Lighting of Commercial Buildings'' ([[Swiss Federal Office of Energy]], 1994).

== Distinctions ==
=== Awards ===
Scartezzini is the recipient of 2018 Nonimaging Optics Best Paper Award (San Diego/USA 2019) by the International Society for Optics and [[Photonics]] (SPIE),<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Gong|first1=Jing|last2=Kostro|first2=André|last3=Scartezzini|first3=Jean-Louis|last4=Schüler|first4=Andreas|title=Nonimaging Optics: Efficient Design for Illumination and Solar Concentration XV |chapter=Feasibility study on a novel daylighting system with embedded micro compound parabolic concentrators (CPCS) |editor1-first=Eli|editor1-last=Yablonovitch|editor2-first=Roland|editor2-last=Winston|date=14 September 2018|chapter-url=https://www.spiedigitallibrary.org/conference-proceedings-of-spie/10758/1075807/Feasibility-study-on-a-novel-daylighting-system-with-embedded-micro/10.1117/12.2320478.short|publisher=International Society for Optics and Photonics|volume=10758|page=1075807|doi=10.1117/12.2320478|bibcode=2018SPIE10758E..07G|isbn=978-1-5106-2087-2|s2cid=116492378 |url=https://infoscience.epfl.ch/handle/20.500.14299/153302 }}</ref> 2017 Outstanding Paper Award at the International Conference on Advanced Electromaterials (ICAE),<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Perera|first1=A. T. D.|last2=Coccolo|first2=Silvia|last3=Scartezzini|first3=Jean-Louis|last4=Mauree|first4=Dasaraden|date=15 July 2018|title=Quantifying the impact of urban climate by extending the boundaries of urban energy system modeling|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306261918305464|journal=Applied Energy|language=en|volume=222|pages=847–860|doi=10.1016/j.apenergy.2018.04.004|bibcode=2018ApEn..222..847P |s2cid=92982851 |issn=0306-2619}}</ref> 2015 Prix SIA Section vaudoise,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Projet De Master (PDM)|url=https://www.epfl.ch/schools/enac/education/fr/architecture/projet-de-master-pdm/|access-date=2021-02-12|website=www.epfl.ch|language=fr-FR|archive-date=3 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210503005542/https://www.epfl.ch/schools/enac/education/fr/architecture/projet-de-master-pdm/}}</ref> 2013 Solar Energy Best Paper Award,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Joly|first1=Martin|last2=Antonetti|first2=Yannik|last3=Python|first3=Martin|last4=Gonzalez|first4=Marina|last5=Gascou|first5=Thomas|last6=Scartezzini|first6=Jean-Louis|last7=Schüler|first7=Andreas|date=1 August 2013|title=Novel black selective coating for tubular solar absorbers based on a sol–gel method|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0038092X13001928|journal=Solar Energy|language=en|volume=94|pages=233–239|doi=10.1016/j.solener.2013.05.009|bibcode=2013SoEn...94..233J|issn=0038-092X|url-access=subscription}}</ref> the 2001/2002 [[European Solar Prize]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Swiss Solar Pavilion at PV EXPO 2011|url=https://www.eda.admin.ch/dam/countries/countries-content/japan/en/Swiss%20Solar%20Pavilion%20at%20PV%20EXPO%202011%20(compact).pdf|website=}}</ref> and the Welsh-Weston bronze medal of the Chartered Institution of Building and Service Engineers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Honorary Fellows and Medallists|url=https://www.cibse.org/building-services/building-services-awards/honorary-fellows-and-medallists|website=CIBSE}}</ref>

He is a Valued Associate Editor at the journal [[Solar Energy (journal)|Solar Energy]] (since 2008),<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/solar-energy|title=Solar Energy}}</ref> Guest Editor for special issues related to CISBAT international conference cycle in the Journal of Physics: Conference Series (2019), Energy Procedia (2017), Energy and Building (1999, 2001, 2011), Solar Energy (2003, 2005, 2007) and an Honorary Member of the Swiss Solar Energy Society (since 1995).<ref>{{Cite web|title=Home|url=https://www.sses.ch/de/|access-date=2021-02-12|website=SSES|language=de-DE}}</ref>

=== Memberships ===
He has been a member of board of the Swiss Competence Center for Energy Research on Future Energy Efficient Buildings and Districts (2013–2020),<ref>{{Cite web|date=11 November 2014|title=Board {{!}} SCCER FEEB&D|url=https://www.sccer-feebd.ch/about-us/peoples/|access-date=2021-02-15|language=en-US|archive-date=2 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602214843/https://www.sccer-feebd.ch/about-us/peoples/}}</ref> member of Swiss Academy of Arts and Sciences (since 2018),<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Smith|first=Barbara|date=2 August 2018|title=Jean-Louis Scartezzini elected to Swiss Academies of Arts & Sciences|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/jean-louis-scartezzini-elected-to-swiss-academies-/|language=en}}</ref> speaker of International Daylight Academy (since 2016),<ref>{{Cite web|title=Swiss Academies of Arts and Sciences – Energy Commission a+|url=http://4dweb.proclim.ch/4dcgi/energy/all/Detail_Person?12098|access-date=2021-02-15|website=4dweb.proclim.ch}}</ref> member of WEF Global Agenda Council on Sustainable Energy (2007–2008),<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=ORCID|title=Jean-Louis Scartezzini (0000-0001-8892-2592)|url=https://orcid.org/0000-0001-8892-2592|access-date=2021-02-15|website=orcid.org|language=en}}</ref> chairman of Research Commission of the Swiss Competence Centre for Energy and Mobility (2005–2014),<ref name=":1" /> member of the energy committee of the Swiss Academy for Engineering Sciences (1999–2007), national liaison officer for Switzerland in the ISES Europe board of directors (1990–1995), president of the Swiss Solar Energy Society (1987–1995) and member of the Swiss Federal experts committee for Solar Energy Applications (1987–1998).

=== Start-ups ===
Scartezzini has been involved in the initiation of several start-up companies such as ShadeMe,<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=ShadeMe|url=https://www.shademe.ch/#about|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210222021829/https://shademe.ch/#about|archive-date=22 February 2021|website=}}</ref> kaemco,<ref>{{Cite web|last=Kämpf|first=Jérôme|date=|title=Publications|url=http://www.kaemco.ch/publications.php|access-date=2021-02-15|website=www.kaemco.ch|language=en}}</ref> SwissINSO,<ref>{{Cite web|title=La plus grande façade solaire au monde|url=https://www.bulletin.ch/de/news-detail/la-plus-grande-facade-solaire-au-monde.html|access-date=2021-02-15|website=www.bulletin.ch|language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=SwissINSO|url=https://www.swissinso.com/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091226205810/http://www.swissinso.com/|archive-date=26 December 2009|access-date=2021-02-15|website=SwissINSO|language=en-US}}</ref> Solstis, Estia,<ref>{{Cite web|title=About Us|url=https://www.estia.ch/copie-de-la-société|access-date=2021-02-15|website=estia|language=fr}}</ref> Rhyner énergie and E4tech Software.<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Partners|url=http://e4tech-software.com/software-partners.html|website=E4tech software}}</ref>

Scartezzini's lab has also issued numerous patents in the field of lighting control, nano-technologies for solar energy conversion and advanced glazing technologies, leading to the launch of start-up and/or spin-off.

=== Press ===
Scartezzini's research was featured in various media outlet such as ''The Daily Californian'',<ref>{{Cite web|last=Staff|first=Nina Narahari {{!}}|date=3 April 2020|title=Study shows energy systems can be impacted by climate change|url=https://www.dailycal.org/2020/04/03/study-shows-energy-systems-can-be-impacted-by-climate-change/|access-date=2021-02-15|website=The Daily Californian|language=en-US}}</ref> [[RTS 1 (Swiss TV channel)|RTS]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=Le changement climatique bouleversera les systèmes énergétiques – Radio|url=https://www.rts.ch/play/radio/cqfd/audio/le-changement-climatique-bouleversera-les-systemes-energetiques?id=11069477|access-date=2021-02-15|website=Play RTS| date=19 February 2020 |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=3 February 2020|title=La moitié des toits suisses pourraient produire de l'électricité|url=https://www.rts.ch/info/sciences-tech/11064301-la-moitie-des-toits-suisses-pourraient-produire-de-lelectricite.html|access-date=2021-02-15|website=rts.ch|language=fr}}</ref> Environment Magazine,<ref>{{Cite web|title=La nécessaire adaptation des énergies renouvelables au changement climatique|url=https://www.environnement-magazine.fr/energie/article/2020/02/18/127991/necessaire-adaptation-des-energies-renouvelables-changement-climatique|access-date=2021-02-15|website=www.environnement-magazine.fr}}</ref> [[Neue Zürcher Zeitung|NZZ]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=3 February 2020|title=Jedes zweite Dach in der Schweiz wäre für Solaranlagen geeignet|url=https://www.nzz.ch/wissenschaft/jedes-zweite-dach-in-der-schweiz-waere-fuer-solaranlagen-geeignet-ld.1538268|website=Neue Zürcher Zeitung}}</ref> and [[Le Temps]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=17 February 2010|title=Avec Jean-Louis Scartezzini, les pionniers sont de retour|language=fr|work=Le Temps|url=https://www.letemps.ch/suisse/jeanlouis-scartezzini-pionniers-retour|access-date=2021-02-15|issn=1423-3967}}</ref>
